summary: Initial integration discovery for Cascade Tech evaluating Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Key topics: SDKs & LangChain/LlamaIndex integration, gateway/proxy architecture, rate limits/quotas, observability/tracing hooks, and enterprise security (SOC2, KMS, VPC). Redwood AE+SE covered deployment options and next steps include sample code, pricing, and a technical deep dive for Dedicated options.
topics: Observability hooks: tracing, token-level cost breakdown
Security: SOC2, KMS, VPC/private deployments, audit logs
transcript:
[00:00] Olivia Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we really appreciate the time. quick intro from our side: I'm Olivia, AE for Redwood Inference, and Diego Morales is our solutions engineer.
[00:08] Karen Liu: Hi all - Karen here, Head of ML at Cascade Tech. Marcus (platform) and Tanya (security) are on as well, and Evan, our PM.
[00:14] Diego Morales: Nice to meet you. high level today we want to map how you plan to integrate - SDKs, any LangChain/LlamaIndex usage, and whether you want hosted or dedicated/private.
[00:23] Evan Cho: Quick context: we build conversational search for enterprise docs, current stack is AWS, we have a microservices gateway and some functions in Node + Python. latency is important for user experience, but cost matters too.
[00:34] Marcus Reed: For us QPS varies - baseline ~30 req/s, peaks of 150 sustained for a few hours during reports. typical prompt size 600-1,200 tokens, some long context retrievals up to 4k.
[00:48] Olivia Park: Great, that helps. Diego, can you outline integration paths?
[00:53] Diego Morales: Sure. three common patterns: 1) direct call to Hosted API via our SDKs (JS/Python/Go), 2) use Redwood behind your gateway/proxy where you keep auth and routing internal, 3) Dedicated or Private deployment where the inference capacity lives in your VPC or on-prem.
[01:10] Karen Liu: For LangChain - we've prototyped with both LangChain and LlamaIndex. we rely on LlamaIndex to build context stores. how opinionated are your connectors? is there an official LangChain chain or do we have to adapt?
[01:23] Diego Morales: We have official client libraries and a LangChain connector example in our repo. it's pretty plug-and-play: the SDK exposes streaming and function-calling semantics that LangChain can consume. for LlamaIndex, there are example adapters; some customers fork a small wrapper to handle multi-turn caching. I'll share the repo.
[01:38] Tanya Patel: Security - we can't send PII to third parties for many customers. what are the hosting controls? we need SOC2 type 2, KMS integration, and audit logs.
[01:47] Olivia Park: Redwood offers Hosted with encryption at rest and in transit, SOC2 attestation, and customer-managed KMS for Dedicated/Private. for PII-heavy workloads, most enterprise customers choose Dedicated or Private so keys and network controls stay in their VPC.
[02:01] Marcus Reed: If we choose Hosted, is there an IP allowlist or static egress we can rely on? we want to connect from our GW only.
[02:07] Diego Morales: Hosted has CIDR ranges for allowlisting and we support mTLS for specific enterprise tiers. For strict network controls, Dedicated in your VPC is the cleanest option.
[02:17] Karen Liu: On the gateway/proxy pattern - we'd prefer to keep a single outbound from our infra to Redwood, so we can centralize rate limits and logging. Does Redwood expect clients to do retry/batching or can you handle batching on the service side?
[02:29] Diego Morales: The runtime supports continuous batching on the server side - we batch compatible requests to improve GPU utilization. that said, customers often build client-side batching for micro-batching to control latency deterministically. we also have a prefix/KV cache you can enable to reduce repeated context cost.
[02:44] Evan Cho: Do you have suggestions for batching window config? our tail latency target is 300ms for the first token.
[02:50] Diego Morales: For that SLA you'd likely keep small client-side batches (1-4) and enable server-side batching with strict latency SLOs. we can tune kernel selection based on seq length distribution. we'll need sample traffic to recommend exact settings.
[03:05] Tanya Patel: Quotas and rate limiting - need to understand how usage throttling appears to us. we don't want silent throttles causing errors in the UX.
[03:13] Olivia Park: Redwood exposes per-key rate limit headers and a quota API. when throttling happens we return explicit 429s and a header with retry-after and current usage. you can also set per-route limits and alerting in the Console.
[03:24] Marcus Reed: For Dedicated, what's the billing model? committed capacity? or per-token?
[03:29] Olivia Park: Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly commits (and overage rates). Hosted is pay-as-you-go per token with volume discounts. we'll send a pricing comparison sheet.
[03:38] Karen Liu: Observability - we need tracing to tie user request to token-level cost and model choices. can we pull per-request latency and token counts?
[03:45] Diego Morales: Yes - Console exposes request traces, per-token cost breakdown, and you can forward traces to your systems via webhooks or export to Datadog/Prometheus. we also have open telemetry support for correlation IDs.
[03:57] Evan Cho: Integration with our existing tracing is a must. are instrumentations in the SDK or do we rely on middleware?
[04:03] Diego Morales: SDKs emit trace hooks; you can attach your trace IDs when calling. for server-side traces we expose the trace ID in response headers so you can correlate end-to-end.
[04:13] Karen Liu: A practical question - can we run a quick benchmark to compare Hosted vs a Dedicated pool you provision? we want to measure latency under our workload and verify quality drift.
[04:23] Olivia Park: Absolutely. typical pilot is a 2-week benchmark: we provide a test key, you run traffic (we can provide scripts), and we help interpret results. if you want Dedicated preview we'll stand up a small reserved pool for the test.
[04:34] Marcus Reed: How heavy is the setup for Dedicated? we have infra constraints and need to know ops burden.
[04:39] Diego Morales: Deployment options: 1) Redwood-managed Dedicated: we host in a cloud account but isolate your capacity and keys, minimal ops on your side. 2) VPC Dedicated: we deploy in your VPC with IAM roles and customer-managed KMS - needs a bit more infra work but gives you full network control. 3) Private on-prem - more involved and usually for large regulated customers.
[04:58] Tanya Patel: KMS integration - if we own the keys in Dedicated in our VPC, do you ever see plaintext?
[05:03] Olivia Park: No - customer-managed KMS means keys never leave your control; Redwood can be configured to never have decryption access. for hosted we can use our KMS but we also offer bring-your-own-key for some enterprise tiers. we'll send the security whitepaper.
[05:16] Karen Liu: Regarding LangChain and LlamaIndex adapters - any gotchas? our previous prototype had repeat tokens because the KV cache wasn't kept between calls.
[05:25] Diego Morales: The KV cache persists across sessions in Dedicated/Private and can be enabled on Hosted to some extent depending on the plan. for multi-turn with LlamaIndex you want to materialize indices and use embedding caching; we have middleware snippets to avoid redundant tokens.
[05:38] Evan Cho: About embeddings - we use embeddings heavily. how do you handle embedding storage, versioning, and retrieval? any managed vector store?
[05:46] Diego Morales: Redwood doesn't provide a managed vector DB today; we integrate with common vector stores (Pinecone, Milvus, Weaviate). we do version embeddings by model ID and expose model fingerprints so you can know which embedding model was used.
[05:58] Marcus Reed: Any restrictions on function calling and streaming? our UX uses early token rendering.
[06:03] Diego Morales: We support streaming with chunked responses and function-calling semantics. there are limits per request depending on model and sequence length, we'll share the specifics.
[06:11] Karen Liu: Compliance: do you rotate certs, and what's your retention policy for logs? some customers need 30-90 day retention for audit-readiness.
[06:19] Olivia Park: Defaults are 30 days for request logs on Hosted, longer retention can be purchased. for Dedicated in your VPC you control logs retention and we can ship audit logs to your SIEM.
[06:29] Evan Cho: Any pitfalls we should watch for during the integration - e.g. quota spikes, billing surprises?
[06:34] Diego Morales: Common pitfalls: unbounded retries causing spike usage (we recommend exponential backoff and idempotency keys), embedding churn when models change, and not enabling prefix caching for repeated contexts which increases token cost. we'll help you set alerts and budget controls.
[06:50] Marcus Reed: We use an internal gateway that handles auth. I'd like to proxy all calls to Redwood through it, adding tracing and rate limits. do you have guidance for that architecture?
[06:59] Diego Morales: Yes, that's a common pattern. you can use your gateway to inject headers for routing and customer IDs; Redwood supports per-route quotas and per-customer keys. just watch for additional hop latency; we can help determine whether to batch before proxying or let the runtime batch server-side.
[07:16] Karen Liu: Do you support webhook callbacks when a long-running generation completes? some of our flows are async.
[07:21] Olivia Park: We offer async job endpoints and webhook callbacks for completions. you can also poll the status API.
[07:27] Evan Cho: Since we do heavy multi-tenant prompting, is there a tenant isolation model for shared Dedicated?
[07:34] Diego Morales: For Dedicated we can partition pools by tenant or use single pool with per-tenant quotas and request tagging. for stricter isolation you can provision separate pools or go Private.
[07:45] Tanya Patel: About data residency - some EU customers require data to remain in eu-west-1. is that supported?
[07:49] Olivia Park: Yes, Redwood has regional control for Dedicated and Hosted in major regions. for strict residency, Dedicated in a region or Private are recommended.
[07:58] Marcus Reed: On-rate limits: can we set per-route burst allowances? say a high-priority path that can go above baseline for short intervals.
[08:05] Diego Morales: Yes, we support burst buckets and burst policies per route. you can define steady-state limits and bursts with automatic backoffs.
[08:13] Karen Liu: Will you help with model selection and quantization? we're sensitive to cost but don't want quality drops.
[08:19] Olivia Park: Redwood Optimize will provide model/quantization recommendations based on your evals. part of the pilot we can run quality checks and suggest quantization profiles that balance cost/latency with quality.
[08:30] Evan Cho: For the pilot, what's the minimal instrumentation we need? i.e., keys, a small test harness?
[08:36] Diego Morales: We'll give you a test key and sample scripts (LangChain/LlamaIndex examples and a benchmark harness). instrumentation: add request IDs, token usage headers, and an optional trace ID - that will let us correlate results.
[08:48] Tanya Patel: How are secrets managed in the SDK? do you recommend environment variables or Vault integration?
[08:53] Diego Morales: SDKs read from env vars by default, but we have instructions for HashiCorp Vault/KMS integrations for secure rotation.
[08:59] Marcus Reed: Suppose we run into a sudden token spike during a customers' audit. can you auto-scale? what's the cold start behavior?
[09:06] Olivia Park: Dedicated can be configured with autoscale and burst capacity. cold start for large models can add a couple hundred ms for first token in some cases; we recommend warm pools for low-latency SLAs.
[09:17] Karen Liu: Any limitations with LlamaIndex context sizes? we sometimes stitch many docs into a single query.
[09:23] Diego Morales: We recommend chunking and vector retrieval to limit prompt size. runtime handles long context up to model max seq length but cost and latency grow. use embeddings + retrieval to keep prompts compact.
[09:35] Evan Cho: It'd be helpful to get a sample Proxy config - e.g., how to forward user-id and trace headers and how to inject idempotency keys.
[09:42] Diego Morales: We'll include a gateway/proxy example in the repo (NGINX + Node + Redwood SDK snippet).
[09:49] Olivia Park: Quick recap: we'll send pricing, security docs, and a sample repo. Diego will share the LangChain/LlamaIndex examples and a benchmark script. Tanya will provide security questions. Marcus will send traffic profile. And we'll schedule the technical deep dive next week.
[10:05] Karen Liu: sounds good. one last concern - do you do red-team style tests or third-party pen tests?
[10:11] Olivia Park: Yes, Redwood has third-party pen tests and can share summaries; full reports are under NDA. we'll attach the compliance pack.
[10:18] Marcus Reed: Great. thanks, everyone.
[10:22] Evan Cho: Thanks - we'll look out for the docs and repo.
[10:25] Tanya Patel: Thanks. some of my security questions will come through separately.
[10:28] Olivia Park: Thanks all, we'll follow up with materials and proposed times for the deep dive. bye.
[10:32] (call ends)

Notes: transcription contains occasional mis-hearings; some product names rendered as "prefix/KV cache" or "KV cache". References to LangChain and LlamaIndex benignly interchanged in places by speakers.
